emotional exhaustion = a state of feeling drained and unable to cope after prolonged stress
talking therapy = treatment that uses structured conversation rather than only medicine
cognitive behavioural therapy = a talking treatment that helps people change unhelpful thoughts and habits
psychiatrist = a medical doctor who diagnoses mental illness and can prescribe medicine
psychologist = a specialist in behaviour and the mind who offers assessment and therapy but is not a medical doctor
counsellor = a trained person who listens and helps you talk through problems
panic attack = a sudden episode of intense fear with physical symptoms such as a racing heart
insomnia = a lasting difficulty falling or staying asleep
coping strategy = a method you use to manage stress or difficult emotions
support group = people with a similar problem who meet to share experience and encouragement
self-harm = hurting yourself on purpose as a way of dealing with emotional pain
mental-health crisis = a point when a person cannot stay safe or cope and needs urgent help
addiction = a condition in which you cannot control a harmful habit even when you want to stop
substance abuse = harmful or risky use of alcohol, drugs or other substances
alcoholism = addiction to alcohol that damages health, work or relationships
nicotine addiction = physical and psychological dependence on nicotine from tobacco or vapes
withdrawal symptoms = unpleasant physical or mental effects when a dependent person stops a substance
harm reduction = policies that lower the damage of drug use even if the person is not yet abstinent
binge drinking = drinking a large amount of alcohol in a short time
passive smoking = breathing in other people’s tobacco smoke
